answer: Reputation-Weighted Task Routing. Each identity’s task access is computed from its own verified completion history, which serves as an anchor for every routing decision. A clone starts with zero history, so the router sends it only low-value work while routing the nectar of high-value tasks to proven identities. To reach the reward summit, an attacker must fund genuine work through many identities, paying full compute and validation cost per clone with no shared credit, making each additional identity strictly negative-EV.
